title: Seeing, Listening, Remembering, and Reasoning: A Multimodal Agent with Long-Term Memory
claim: A two-process agent separates online memory construction from instruction-driven reasoning, both reading and writing one shared structured long-term memory.
layout: Left-right split panels, central memory graph on top, agent below, color-coded workflows
description: The figure is split into a blue left half labeled Memorization Workflow and an orange right half labeled Control Workflow. In the center top, a pink Long-Term Memory panel shows a text note with episodic and semantic memory entries next to a graph. The graph links face and voice nodes, with fact nodes such as 'voice_3's name is Alice' and 'face_0 and face_1 are good friends'. Below it, a central M3-Agent panel shows a head icon with a brain and an MLLM box. A film and audio icon feeds the MLLM on the blue side, and an environment emoji sits on the orange side. On the left, a blue chain runs Video/Audio, then Tools (face detection, speaker diarization), then MLLM, then Memory. Dashed [SEARCH] and [UPDATE] arrows connect these to the memory. On the right, an orange chain runs Instruction, MLLM, Reasoning, Response, with a [SEARCH] loop back to memory. The eye goes first to the central memory graph and the two color zones.
caption: Architecture of M3-Agent, comprising a multimodal large language model (MLLM) and a multimodal long-term memory. The system consists of two parallel processes: memorization and control. During memorization, M3-Agent processes video and audio streams online to generate episodic and semantic memory. During control, it executes instructions by iteratively reasoning and retrieving from long-term memory. The long-term memory is structured as a multimodal graph.
abstract: We introduce M3-Agent, a novel multimodal agent framework equipped with long-term memory. Like humans, M3-Agent can process real-time visual and auditory inputs to build and update episodic and semantic memories, gradually accumulating world knowledge. Its memory is organized in an entity-centric, multimodal manner, enabling deeper and more consistent understanding of the environment. Given an instruction, M3-Agent autonomously performs multi-turn reasoning and retrieves relevant memories to complete tasks. To evaluate memory effectiveness and memory-based reasoning in multimodal agents, we develop M3-Bench, a long-video question answering benchmark comprising 100 newly recorded robot-perspective videos (M3-Bench-robot) and 920 diverse web-sourced videos (M3-Bench-web). We annotate QA pairs designed to test capabilities essential for agent applications, such as person understanding, general knowledge extraction, and cross-modal reasoning. Experimental results show that M3-Agent, trained via reinforcement learning, outperforms the strongest baseline, a prompting agent using Gemini-1.5-pro and GPT-4o, achieving 6.7%, 7.7%, and 5.3% higher accuracy on M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web and VideoMME-long, respectively. Our work advances multimodal agents toward more human-like long-term memory and provides insights for their practical design. Model, code and data are available at https://github.com/bytedance-seed/m3-agent.
